mathlib_match.how: One declaration per clause, specialized to the already given strong monoidal braided functor F=p_X^*. Clause 1: CategoryTheory.Functor.monObjObj, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Mon.lean:827–836, gives a MonObj on F.obj Lambda with one := epsilon F followed by F.map eta and mul := LaxMonoidal.mu F Lambda Lambda followed by F.map mu. The defining equations obj.η_def and obj.μ_def at lines 844–847 identify exactly eta_X and mu_X of det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients-definition. Clause 2: CategoryTheory.Functor.mapMon, Mon.lean:867–869, is the functor with object F.obj A.X and morphism F.map f.hom; map.instIsMonHom at lines 850–852 gives preservation of unit and multiplication. Clause 3: CategoryTheory.Functor.isCommMonObj_obj, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/CommMon_.lean:157–159, preserves commutativity under F.LaxBraided; mapCommMon at lines 169–176 packages the same construction. Read Mon.lean:73–84, 815–875 and CommMon_.lean:146–176. MonObj is the tensor-monoid convention for ring objects, not cartesian RingObj. F.LaxMonoidal and F.LaxBraided follow from the strong monoidal braided structure already supplied as input by def-sfb-upper-star-from-point and the coefficient definition. The source and target have the sheafified tensor over Z. This does not construct p_X^* or prove its monoidality; those remain statement dependencies through the coefficient definition. No hypothesis on X, no commutativity for clauses 1–2, and no change of coefficient category is needed.
